title: PayG flipbook — lifetime scenarios and unit-econ sketches
content:
Notes to self — very rough flipbook of lifecycle scenarios (PAYG-heavy) + token math / amortization. Keep it cramped, want a couple quick outcomes to show to product tomorrow.

Context / goal:
- Idea: small PAYG-first funnel (low friction), but strong heuristics to nudge into short commitments when economics look good.
- Want to compare 3 starter patterns across 3 lifetimes (fast-churn, mid-retain, sticky).
- Translate to: gross margin per user-month, CAC payback, and 90-day LTV.

Assumptions (base numbers — tweakable):
- Average tokens per active-user-day (TAUD): 15k tokens
- Days active per month: 8 days
- Effective tokens/month = 15k * 8 = 120k tokens/month per active user
- Hosted cost per 1M prompt+completion tokens (avg) = $1.10 (includes infra + model op cost, approximated) => $0.0000011 per token
- Variable cost per user/month = 120k * $0.0000011 = $0.132 (seems tiny; but includes only token compute; add caching/overhead multiplier)
- Add overhead multiplier for infra, cache miss, routing, storage = x3.5 => variable op cost = $0.46/mo (~$5.5/yr)
- Payment processing & support alloc ~ $0.20/mo per user at scale
- Total variable cost per active user-month ~= $0.66 

Quick monetization tiers to test: (PAYG + tiny subscription anchors)
A) Pure PAYG: $0.00002 per token billed (2 cents per 1k tokens) => for 120k tokens => $2.40/mo
B) Micro-sub: $5/mo includes 300k tokens then $0.000015 per extra token. (Good for mid usage)
C) Session bundle: $15/mo for 1,000,000 tokens + higher concurrency SLO (sell to small teams)

Back-of-envelope margin per user-month: (use var cost $0.66)
- Plan A revenue = 120k * 0.00002 = $2.40 => contribution = $1.74 (72% margin)
- Plan B revenue = $5 (fits under inclusive bucket) => contribution = $4.34 (87% margin)
- Plan C revenue (if churned avg) = $15 => contribution = $14.34 (95% margin)

But these look optimistic because we undercount: reserved capacity overhead for high concurrency, support, fraud, billing. Add fixed amortized cost per active user (S): $1.50/mo for small customers to cover non-token ops. Recompute: contribution A = $0.24, B = $2.84, C = $12.84. More realistic.

Lifetime scenarios (monthly churn / retention):
- Fast churn: M = 10% churn => Avg life ~ 10 months
- Mid retain: M = 5% churn => Avg life ~ 20 months
- Sticky: M = 2% churn => Avg life ~ 50 months

Assume CAC (paid + sales-assisted) funnel average: paid CAC = $18 (self-serve), assisted CAC = $600 (enterprise). We'll use paid funnel for these starters.

LTV calc (90-day and asymptotic): use contribution margin (after var + fixed S), discount ignored for short horizon.
Scenario table (paid CAC $18):
- Fast churn, Plan A: monthly contrib $0.24 => LTV = 0.24 * 10 = $2.4 (bad, CAC negative) => need conversion to B/C or upsell fast
- Mid, Plan B: monthly contrib $2.84 => LTV = 56.8 => CAC payback ~6 months (reasonable)
- Sticky, Plan C: monthly contrib $12.84 => LTV = 642 => CAC payback <2 months

Interpretation / tactics:
- Pure PAYG anchored at $0.00002/token too low for sustainable CAC unless conversion/expansion rates are high. Use as acquisition magnet but must nudge usage into subscription within ~60–90 days.
- Micro-sub ($5) hits best balance for early-stage SMBs. Push via UI default, trial top-ups, session-bundles.
- Offer trial credits that mimic $12–15 value (enough to try up to ~500k tokens) to trigger activation; but ensure amortized credit cost baked into early campaigns (credits consumed * effective token cost).

Activation flow experiments to test (cheap A/Bs):
- A: Offer 300k token free credit, require CC on file. Measure conversion to $5 micro-sub in 30d.
- B: No CC, smaller credit (100k), prompt for CC at 50% consumption.
- C: Offer 3-day high-rate voucher (double throughput) to illustrate value, then present micro-sub.

Key open questions / sensitivity knobs:
- Effective per-token cost varies a lot with model mix (embeddings vs chat vs LLM). Need model-weighted token rate vector. Add quick vector later.
- Cache effect: prefix-heavy workloads can lower effective token cost by up to 40% depending on shared cache. We'll need simple bucket: cache-friendly, interactive, and long-form.
- Burst cost: for low-latency SLOs we may need reserved capacity — add surcharge or put into subscription.

Quick token-to-GPU-hour sanity check (for capacity planning):
- Rough throughput: 1 A100-equivalent GPU produces ~2.5M tokens/hr for local autoregressive inference under our optimized runtime (numbers for pricing planning only).
- So 1M tokens ~= 0.4 GPU-hr. If GPU-hour cost (cloud) = $3.5/hr reserved => cost per 1M tokens raw infra = $1.4; this is higher than our earlier $1.10 assumption. But with batching and KV cache, effective can drop to $0.6–0.9 per M.
- For hosted pricing we should keep a conservative baseline of $1.20 per M tokens for financial planning.

Consequences if baseline = $1.20/M:
- Per token cost = $0.0000012 -> variable monthly (120k tokens) = $0.144 -> times overhead x3 => $0.50 var cost + $1.50 fixed => ~ $2.00 true cost per active user-month. That kills Plan A economics (2.40 rev -> 0.40 contribution) but Plan B/C still ok.

Product decisions to consider (short list):
- Default to micro-sub ($5) as onboarding anchor, make PAYG a visible toggle but default off.
- Use trial credit sized to nudge users into second month conversion. Design credit as limited to non-enterprise features (no reserved concurrency).
- Explicitly surface upgrade path when usage crosses 300k tokens in 7d (trigger banner + discount).
- Surface estimated token-cost to customers in console (helps set expectations).

TODO / next steps:
- Get model-weighted token cost matrix from applied-ml (ask Evan) -> fill in vector for gpt-3-like, open-chat, embeddings.
- Run simple pricing sim (Monte Carlo) for 10k users with randomized churn and expansion — quick script. (Priya to help with assumptions.)
- Capture real-world token distribution from last 30 days for onboarding cohort -> measure median tokens/day, 95p, 99p.
- Draft microcopy for credit UX and CC-on-file flows.

Notes (random):
- If we can identify early power users (top 5% token usage in first 14 days) we can send personalized offers (discounted commit) that could improve LTV/CAC tradeoff.
- Consider combo: $5 micro-sub + low unit token price (loss leader) vs plain PAYG (higher price). Test both.

Open hypotheses to vet: (for experiments)
1) Small CC-on-file credit drives >20% conversion to micro-sub within 30d.
2) 300k credit is optimal (enough to reach aha) vs 100k (not enough).
3) Customers who hit 300k tokens in first week have >3x retention vs baseline.

Quick comms plan for tomorrow: one slide with 3 scenario buckets, 2 supporting calcs (baseline unit cost and LTV), 3 recommended experiments. Use this doc as speaker notes.

End of flipbook — save and iterate when we have model-weighted costs.

Rough scratch sums below (for copy-paste):
- tokens/month: 120,000
- base cost per 1M tokens: $1.20 -> per token $0.0000012
- var cost per month: 0.144 -> overhead x3 = 0.432 -> round .43
- fixed amortized S: 1.50 => total cost ~1.93
- pricing anchors: PAYG $0.00002/token (2c/1k), micro $5/300k, team $15/1M

-- maya
